subject: Hong Kong pilot: proposal for region-specific dedicated pool & SKU rebalancing
body_preview: Request for a Hong Kong dedicated pilot pool, SKU asks + residency, procurement timeline; internal sizing discussion proposing hybrid A100/A10 mix and fallback in Singapore.
messages:
From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@orientai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Zhao <emma_zhao@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: HK pilot: dedicated pool ask and timeline

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. OrientAI is ready to pilot Redwood Dedicated for a Hong Kong-based inference lane tied to our Finlytics integration. High level ask: a small dedicated pool for Q1 pilot (6–10 sustained inference workers) with data residency in Hong Kong.

What we need to confirm from Redwood:
- SKU options and cost for an initial 3-month pilot (we expect peak token throughput of ~45M tokens/day, QPS peaking ~120 req/s, avg sequence 512 tokens).
- Options for mixing higher-end cards vs cheaper throughput-friendly nodes (we care about latency 95th under 250ms).
- Timeline for provisioning + any required procurement docs (SOW, PO, SOC references).

I've attached an initial traffic profile and rough procurement checklist. Procurement at Orient has asked us to loop in HKCloud (our local infra partner) for the pilot hosting — copying their procurement alias.

Can the team share SKU guidance and an initial proposal by early next week?

Appreciate it —
Simon

Attachments: hk-pilot-sku-estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet), pilot-architecture-diagram.png (image)

--
Simon Lee
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships, OrientAI
Simon.Lee@orientai.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@orientai.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, procure@hkcloudcorp.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HK pilot: dedicated pool ask and timeline

Simon — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic profile. Looping in Hannah (capacity planning) and Karthik (regional ops) to surface concrete SKU mixes and a provisioning timeline. A few clarifying questions that will change the SKU mix:

1) Latency SLO target: you mentioned 95th under 250ms — is that for single-turn completions (no tool calls) or does it include end-to-end app amplification (tooling/reranking)?
2) Persistence: do you need warm KV cache per-customer (stateful) or are requests stateless? If stateful we recommend fewer, larger nodes to keep KV in-GPU.
3) Residency and compliance: Hong Kong residency is noted — do you need an auditable KMS/HSM in-region or will regional key escrow suffice?
4) Procurement cadence: does OrientAI want Redwood to invoice to Orient directly, or will HKCloud act as a reseller and bill?

Quick take: for the traffic you flagged, a cost/latency sweet spot is a hybrid starting pool: 4x A100 80GB (for low-latency critical traffic) + 8x A10 equivalent capacity for high-throughput, best-effort workloads. That lets us hit the 95th requirement on critical routes while keeping unit costs lower. Will formalize numbers and a SOW draft.

Can you confirm the above so we can finalize the SKU spreadsheet and SLA carve-outs?

Thanks —
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Simon Lee <simon.lee@orientai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 14:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HK pilot: dedicated pool ask and timeline

Marcus / Simon —

Following Marcus' questions, here's a pragmatic provisioning proposal we can deliver in 3 weeks (pilot start target):

- Pilot pool composition (initial):
  - 4 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (pinned for low-latency routes, reserved)
  - 8 x NVIDIA A10 / equivalent (shared, preemptible-friendly for bulk inference)
  - Total effective concurrency: ~160 concurrent short-run requests (profile dependent)

- Why this split: A100s will serve the 95th latency-sensitive traffic and stateful cache; A10-equivalents handle bulk throughput and reduce cost. If Orient prefers fewer big cards, swap two A10s for one additional A100 (with corresponding token cost delta).

- Fallback & geo-safety: We recommend cross-region standby in Singapore (sin) in case of Hong Kong provider maintenance; we can route non-sensitive traffic there with a transparent fallback policy.

- Compliance/Keys: We can support regional key escrow for pilot. For audited KMS/HSM in-region we need legal sign-off and add ~2 weeks to delivery.

I'll attach a quick cost delta snapshot and a short SOW boilerplate for Marcus to send externally.

Hannah

Attachments: sla-exception-draft.pdf (draft)

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HK pilot: dedicated pool ask and timeline

Quick operational notes from ops side:

- Provisioning window: if we agree on SKU and SOW by EOD Nov 3, we can hit a soft provision (network + control plane config) by Nov 20 and full GPU provisioning by Dec 1. That assumes no audited HSM requirement.
- Node placement: Hong Kong colos currently have limited A100 capacity; we may need short-term A100 lease from our Singapore pool with in-region peering (adds ~15ms median RTT to GPU calls). If Orient insists on strictly in-region GPUs, lead time may extend by 3–4 weeks.
- Cost levers: enable autoscaling policies with aggressive cold-start cache warmers; this reduces steady-state A100 hours by ~18% in our estimates.

Operational ask: please confirm whether HK residency requirement is a hard constraint or an ideal target. If hard, we'll build the procurement timeline with the longer lead and lock in capacity windows with our colo partners.

-Karthik

Marcus / Simon —

HKCloud can act as reseller for the pilot. For our PO process we need the following to begin:
1) Final SOW (signed PDF) with exact SKU counts and billing entity.
2) Redacted SOC 2 Type II summary (we can accept Redwood's hosted summary for pilot).
3) Invoice remit details and PO template (we've attached our PO template).

Timeline: once we receive (1)-(3) we can issue a PO within 5 business days and kick off colo provisioning. Note that any audited in-region HSM requirement will require an addendum and extend lead time.

We are fine with the A100/A10 hybrid approach; please include a short paragraph on fallback routing to Singapore in the SOW.

Best,
